subject: MSA + Order Form: clarify auto-renew split cycles and TFC scheduling
messages:
From: Mike Larson <mike.larson@brightline.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightline.com
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA & Order Form – termination scheduling questions

Ben —

Thanks for sending over the latest MSA and Order Form drafts. A couple of items our legal/procurement teams flagged that we need to resolve before we proceed to signature:

- Auto-renew: We have multiple Order Forms (pilot, enterprise) and want the pilot to be on a non-auto-renewing 12-week term while the enterprise order auto-renews annually. Can Order Forms be scoped to different renewal mechanics without touching the MSA?
- Termination for Convenience (TFC): Our procurement team prefers a 30-day notice for pilots and a 90-day for enterprise, but your counsel indicated a single notice window in the MSA. Is there a way to have staggered notice windows per Order Form?
- Offboarding obligations: If TFC is exercised on the enterprise order, we need a guarantee of data handoff and a rate-limited export window for 60 days.

We can jump on a quick call; procurement would like a written runbook/plan we can include as an appendix to the Order Form so internal stakeholders have predictable expectations. Also attaching our standard procurement checklist.

Thanks,
Mike Larson
VP, Procurement — Brightline Systems
[Attachment: Brightline_Procurement_Checklist.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mike Larson <mike.larson@brightline.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form – termination scheduling questions

Mike —

Really appreciate the clarity here. Short answer: yes — we can support different renewal mechanics on Order Forms, but we need to ensure nothing in the Order Forms shortens or contradicts the MSA baseline for notice and service obligations. Practical plan I propose:

1) Split-cycle approach: Pilot Order Form = fixed 12-week non-auto-renewing term. Enterprise Order Form = 1-year term with auto-renew.
2) TFC windows: Allow Order Forms to propose notice windows but cap them so they don’t create conflicting operational obligations vs. the MSA; i.e., the MSA retains the overriding termination workflow and audit/logging obligations.
3) Offboarding: We can commit to a 60-day export window for pilot data and a 90-day export window for enterprise with rate limits and a documented handoff checklist (we’ll attach as an appendix).

I’ve uploaded a quick redline that implements the split-cycle language and a draft appendix (redlines_brightline_v1.docx). Karthik — can you check the proposed language below and confirm we’re not exposing any runaway TFC liability?

Proposed Order Form clause (draft):
"Order Forms attached to this Agreement may specify differing Term and Renewal mechanics provided that such mechanics do not shorten the notice or post-termination obligations set forth in the Master Services Agreement. Where Order Forms prescribe alternate notice periods for Termination for Convenience, the parties acknowledge that the Master Services Agreement’s offboarding and data export obligations shall remain effective and controlling to the extent of any conflict."

Available for a 30-minute sync tomorrow (Mon) or Tue — what works for you?

Best,
Ben
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redlines_brightline_v1.docx (docx)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA & Order Form – termination scheduling questions

Ben / Laura —

Quick legal notes after scanning Ben’s draft and Brightline’s asks:

- High level: I agree with the split-cycle approach so long as the MSA contains a clear supremacy / reconciliation clause. We should avoid language that allows an Order Form to effectively shorten MSA notice or warranty obligations.

- Suggested changes to Ben’s proposed clause (redline recommendations):
  * Replace "shall remain effective and controlling to the extent of any conflict" with "shall prevail in the event of any conflict between the Order Form and the MSA." This avoids ambiguity about which obligations are controlling.
  * Add an explicit carveout that TFC on an Order Form cannot create termination liability for previously-billed committed usage (i.e., mid-term commitments are pro-rated per the Order Form’s billing schedule).
  * Add a requirement that any non-standard notice window in an Order Form is subject to prior written approval by Redwood Legal via the Order Form approval workflow. That gives us a gating control to avoid unexpected exposure.

- Offboarding/export: We can commit to a 60-day export window for pilots and 90-day for enterprise as Ben suggested, but add "rate-limited export" language and a fee schedule if export requires above-norm assistance by Redwood Ops.

- Operational ask: laura, please do a short action list for Ops/Onboarding so we can attach the runbook appendix with exact SLAs (export throughput, contact points, acceptance criteria).

If Brightline is open to the approval gating approach, we can propose final redlines that incorporate the supremacy language and the approval step. Happy to draft the final MSA paragraph tonight for Ben to send along.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: Mike Larson <mike.larson@brightline.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightline.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form – termination scheduling questions

Ben / Karthik / Laura —

Thanks — that structure works for us. A few follow-ups from procurement:

- Procurement accepts the split-cycle approach and accepts the supremacy language you suggested. Please send the final redline with the exact supremacy sentence and the approval gating clause.
- Brightline will treat pilots as standalone short-term engagements and is ok with a 60-day export window for pilots. For enterprise we accept 90 days. Procurement will push back on any export fee unless it is clearly documented and reasonable; can you provide a short fee schedule if ops assistance is required?
- We need the final redline by EOD Wed (Apr 7) to keep our procurement cycle on track; otherwise our internal approvals slip into the next month.

I’ve looped procurement@brightline.com for PO timing — they’ll prepare a draft PO once the redlines are accepted.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Mike
VP, Procurement — Brightline Systems
[Attachment: Brightline_PO_Checklist.pdf (pdf)]
snippet: Brightline asks for split auto-renew and staggered TFC windows; legal proposes supremacy + approval gating; external requests final redline by EOD Apr 7.
